newsitem.title: USA: Unocal seen shifting E&P focus to reserves.
newsitem.headline: Unocal seen shifting E&P focus to reserves.

text.p: Unocal Corp will increase capital investment sharply from 1998 through 2001 and analysts said it will focus more on exploration, particularly in the U.S. Gulf, in an effort to rebuild reserves.
Top executives from Unocal unit Spirit Energy 76, a spun-off unit which owns and operates the company's U.S. upstream business, briefed analysts on its plans on Wednesday.
"Between 1998 and 2001 capital expenditures for the lower 48 (United States) could average almost $500 million annually," said David Garcia, a spokesman for Unocal.
That would represent an increase from an expected $330 million this year, he said.
"The strategy is to significantly grow production and reserves through the drillbit and that means exploration," Garcia added.

Spirit may experience a further small dip in production and reserves this year, but by most conservative estimates it would remain flat, Garcia said, adding that Unocal will announce further details on its plans on Friday.
Analysts were cautiously optimistic that the plans could reverse Spirit's falling reserves base.

"The goals outlined at yesterday's meeting appear realistic and credible, given the capital Unocal has committed and the past performance of the management team," said Schroder & Co analyst Michael Mayer in a note to clients on Thursday.

"However, competition is fierce in the Gulf of Mexico and the market will probably not pay for Unocal's potential until the new management team at Spirit is able to announce a few good discoveries," Mayer added.

Spirit, which was formed as part of the reorganization of the company last year when downstream assets were sold off, in recent months hired a number of well-regarded executives with successful track records in finding oil, particularly in the U.S. Gulf.
Unocal's shares closed up 15 cents at $40 on Thursday.
